# 🤖 CouchCMS Documentation AI Toolkit

Complete AI-assisted documentation development system for creating consistent, high-quality technical documentation.

**AI coding agents:** see **[AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)** for repository layout, commands, and which files are generated by `bun run sync`. For one combined check, use **`bun run ai`** (sync + Agent Skill verification + validate).

## 🚀 Quick Start (30 Seconds)

### Convert Any Content to Markdown

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md

Convert this content about editable regions:

[Paste your HTML, text, or notes]
```

### Create New Documentation

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md

Create a new page about [topic] in the [section] section
```

### Check Formatting

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/markdown-quick-reference.md

How do I format [element]?
```

## 🤖 How It Works

### 0. Single Source of Truth (Master Configuration)
**[DOCS-STANDARDS.md](DOCS-STANDARDS.md)** - Master configuration file

All AI editor configurations are automatically generated from this file:
```bash
# Preferred: sync + verify SKILL.md + validate (single pipeline)
bun run ai

# Or step by step
bun run sync
bun run validate

# Same as `bun run ai` (alias)
bun run ai:update
```

💡 **The sync happens automatically** on `bun install` - all AI tools are instantly configured!

### 1. Automated Rules (Passive)
Located in `.cursor/rules/` - these automatically apply when you edit files:

- **[markdown.mdc](.cursor/rules/markdown.mdc)** - Complete formatting rules
- **[content-structure.mdc](.cursor/rules/content-structure.mdc)** - Content organization
- **[component-architecture.mdc](.cursor/rules/component-architecture.mdc)** - Component patterns

💡 **You don't need to do anything** - these work automatically!

### 2. AI Prompts (Active)
Located in `.cursor/prompts/` - use these explicitly when needed:

- **[convert-to-markdown.md](.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md)** - Convert any content
- **[markdown-quick-reference.md](.cursor/prompts/markdown-quick-reference.md)** - Quick syntax lookup

💡 **Reference these with `@` in your prompts**

### 3. Documentation (Reference)
- **[STYLEGUIDE.md](STYLEGUIDE.md)** - Complete authoritative rules
- **[README.md](.cursor/README.md)** - Short hub for `.cursor` rules and prompts only
- **[Prompts README](.cursor/prompts/README.md)** - Detailed usage guide

### 4. Agent Skills (multi-editor)

Optional: install the **CouchCMS Documentation** skill into **Cursor**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, or [other supported agents](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills#supported-agents) using the open [Agent Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) (`bunx skills`). This complements auto-applied Cursor rules and synced files such as `CLAUDE.md`.

| Item | Location |
|------|----------|
| Skill definition | [`skills/couchcms-documentation/SKILL.md`](skills/couchcms-documentation/SKILL.md) |
| Step-by-step guide (pick your editor) | [Agent Skills](https://docs.couchcms.com/miscellaneous/agent-skills/) on the documentation site |
| Remove skill installs | `bun run skills:prune` — passthrough to **`bun x skills remove`** ([`scripts/skills-agent-prune.js`](scripts/skills-agent-prune.js), same UX as [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)) |
| Strip all skills from one agent | `bun run agents:prune -- -a cursor -y` — passthrough to **`bun x skills remove --skill '*'`** ([`scripts/agents-prune.js`](scripts/agents-prune.js)) |
| See which editor/AI folders exist on disk (`.giga`, `.tabnine`, `.agents`, …) | `bun run ai:list` — [`scripts/ai-tooling-inventory.js`](scripts/ai-tooling-inventory.js) |
| Pick multiple folders to remove (interactive) | `bun run ai:list -- --interactive` or **`bun run ai:pick`** (checkbox + arrows; optional `--dry-run`) |

### Local tool folders (inventory)

Run **`bun run ai:list`** to print a **detected list** of known AI/editor directories (sync output, skills CLI installs, optional tools like **`.giga`**). Use **`--json`** for scripts. To **delete** folders you no longer use, run **`--remove <dir> --dry-run`**, then **`--remove <dir> --yes`** (only allowed paths are accepted; **`.cursor`**, **`.vscode`**, and **`.github`** are protected).

**Stop `bun run sync` from recreating** a removed tool folder: add **`ai-sync.exclude.json`** at the repo root (copy [`ai-sync.exclude.example.json`](ai-sync.exclude.example.json)) with a **`skipWrites`** array, **or** use **`bun run ai:list -- --remove .tabnine --yes --sync-exclude`** to delete **`.tabnine`** and record **`tabnine`** in **`ai-sync.exclude.json`** in one step. Valid ids are listed in [`scripts/ai-sync-shared.js`](scripts/ai-sync-shared.js).

```bash
# From the repository root; replace -a with your agent id
bunx skills add . --skill couchcms-documentation -a cursor -y
```

## 📖 Common Use Cases

### Converting Existing Documentation

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md

I have this HTML documentation about editable regions:

<html>
<h1>Editable Regions</h1>
<p>Content here...</p>
</html>
```

**Result:** Properly formatted MDX with:
- Valid frontmatter
- Correct heading hierarchy
- Formatted code examples
- Appropriate admonitions
- Related content links

### Creating Tag Reference

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md

Create a tag reference page for <cms:pages>.

Include:
- Parameter documentation
- Usage examples
- Common patterns
- Related tags
```

### Tutorial Development

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md

Create a tutorial for building a portfolio site.

Structure:
- Part 1: Setup
- Part 2: Templates
- Part 3: Content
```

### Quick Syntax Check

```markdown
@.cursor/prompts/markdown-quick-reference.md

Show me:
1. How to format tag references
2. How to create code blocks with filenames
3. How to add admonitions
```

## 🎓 Learning Path

### For New Authors

1. **Read:** [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (5 minutes)
2. **Try:** Convert a simple piece of content
3. **Reference:** [markdown-quick-reference.md](.cursor/prompts/markdown-quick-reference.md) when needed
4. **Trust:** Let auto-rules handle formatting

### For Experienced Authors

1. **Skim:** [SYSTEM-OVERVIEW.md](SYSTEM-OVERVIEW.md) for architecture, or this file for workflows
2. **Use:** [convert-to-markdown.md](.cursor/prompts/convert-to-markdown.md) for scaffolding
3. **Consult:** [STYLEGUIDE.md](STYLEGUIDE.md) for edge cases
4. **Contribute:** Improve prompts based on experience

## 📊 Quality Standards

All documentation generated by this toolkit meets:

✅ **Content Structure**
- Valid frontmatter with SEO metadata
- Proper heading hierarchy
- Clear introduction and flow
- Document endings with next links

✅ **Text Formatting**
- Correct product terminology
- Technical terms in backticks
- UI elements in bold
- Proper tag and doc references

✅ **Code Examples**
- Descriptive titles
- Proper syntax highlighting
- Complete, working examples
- Preserved formatting

✅ **Accessibility**
- Semantic HTML5
- WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
- Descriptive links
- Image alt text

## 🔧 System Management

### Update AI Configurations
```bash
# Edit the master configuration
vim DOCS-STANDARDS.md

# Recommended: full pipeline (sync + SKILL check + validate)
bun run ai

# Or step by step
bun run sync
bun run validate
```

### Supported AI Tools
The sync system generates configurations for:
- ✅ Cursor AI (`.cursorrules`)
- ✅ Claude AI (`CLAUDE.md`)
- ✅ Windsurf AI (`.windsurfrules`)
- ✅ GitHub Copilot (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`)
- ✅ VS Code (`.vscode/settings.json`)
- ✅ Tabnine (`.tabnine/settings.json`)
- ✅ Amazon CodeWhisperer (`.codewhisperer/settings.json`)
- ✅ Universal EditorConfig (`.editorconfig`)

**All from one file: DOCS-STANDARDS.md** 🎯
